statement: A tree is given as: a line with n, then a line of n level-order entries where -1 marks an absent child; each placed node consumes the next two entries as its left and right children. Print the preorder traversal - root, then the whole left subtree, then the whole right subtree - as space-separated values. Preorder announces every node before anything inside its subtrees, which is why it is the order used to copy or serialise a tree.
constraints: Node values are positive; -1 marks an absent child.

example.why: Root 1 first, then the left subtree 2, 4, 5 under the same discipline, then the right subtree 3.

hint: Three lines: visit, recurse left, recurse right - and the empty tree does nothing.
mistake: Emitting the node between or after the recursions; that is inorder or postorder instead.
